title: Direct matrix swaps through canonical storage
objective: Replace whole-matrix-copy row and column swaps with checked O(n)/O(m) direct mutation for canonical ZZ, QQ, packed small GF(p), and M4RI GF(2) matrices; preserve Sage semantics and prove backend selection and scaling.

oracles: Existing matrix selection implementation as differential oracle
exceptions: Thin host-neutral inline adapters unwrap generated owned resources to mature FLINT/M4RI swap primitives; packed GF(p) remains source-transparent typed Python and no handwritten mathematical algorithm or N-API callback is added.

handoff.summary: Added checked generated FLINT and M4RI row/column swap declarations, host-neutral adapters, source-transparent packed GF(p) kernels, and public in-place routing with cache invalidation and preserved resource identity. Native and disabled-native behavior agree across ZZ, QQ, GF(2), and GF(97); the disabled-native GF(p) path applies the checked semantic plan directly to canonical typed-array storage instead of copying the matrix. Warm 100-swap measurements on 1000x1000 matrices were 8.25/8.52 ms for ZZ rows/columns, 23.01/10.03 ms for QQ, 8.73/8.00 ms for GF(2), and 8.16/10.03 ms for GF(97); a single direct row swap was 19x to 143x faster than the superseded whole-matrix selection strategy. Architecture, strict Python, focused public tests, portable tests, and the 567.94-second full native suite all passed against implementation commit a614e5ff10fd756e17c2d70abdd6a9cf532df855. Generated adapter growth raised the measured native-integration lazy footprint by 7826 bytes, so its ratchet moved minimally from 600000 to 605000 bytes.
risks: The full native validation was linux-x64; macOS ARM64 and Windows fallback behavior remain platform-matrix integration work.

The generated FLINT/M4RI declaration identities change because new functions are part of the canonical deterministic descriptor; reviewers should expect those generated updates rather than treating them as unrelated churn.
next_steps: Review generated declaration identity changes and the public no-copy/storage-identity assertions before integration.
Run the focused swap test and benchmark on the M1 portability host after integration, then add an explicit warm swap budget if cross-host measurements are stable.
